V&A East Museum celebrates making and creativity’s power to bring change. Created with young people and rooted in east London’s heritage, V&A East Museum explores what’s shaping our world with the voices that lead contemporary culture.

The V&A has two sites in the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, [a short walk apart.](https://www.vam.ac.uk/info/va-east-museum-and-va-east-storehouse-walking-route) 
Find out more about [navigating from V&A East Museum to Storehouse](https://www.vam.ac.uk/info/va-east-museum-and-va-east-storehouse-walking-route) , and [visiting V&A East Storehouse](https://www.vam.ac.uk/east/storehouse/visit).

## About V&A East Museum

A powerhouse for innovation, creativity and learning located in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park, featuring five floors exploring how creativity changes the world, rooted in the communities and voices that are shaping global culture right now.

### Galleries

Our **Why We Make** galleries feature over 500 objects spanning centuries and cultures and place works by Leigh Bowery and Althea McNish in direct conversation with new east London acquisitions — past and present, local and global.

### Exhibitions

Our landmark exhibition, [**The Music is Black: A British Story**,](https://www.vam.ac.uk/exhibitions/the-music-is-black-a-british-story) traces British culture through Black British music, from 1900 to now - featuring personal objects from Little Simz, JME and Joan Armatrading, iconic stage costumes, and powerful photography from Jennie Baptiste, Eddie Otchere, Dennis Morris and more.

[Find out more and book tickets](https://www.vam.ac.uk/exhibitions/the-music-is-black-a-british-story)

### upperground DJ sets

Our new DJ residency [_**upperground**_](https://www.vam.ac.uk/event/p9PR3vALR5D/upperground-dj-sets-october-december-2026), invites artists and selectors to activate the museum’s upper ground floor on Thursday evenings. Each edition places the spotlight on one guest DJ, giving them space to develop an extended set through their own musical language.

[Discover who's up next on upperground](https://www.vam.ac.uk/event/p9PR3vALR5D/upperground-dj-sets-october-december-2026)

## Getting here

V&A East Museum has two public entrances:

**Lower Ground entrance** – located on Aquatic Walk, directly in front of Tallow Bridge

Coordinates: 51°32'30.3"N 0°00'49.9"W

what3words: [loudly.maker.extra](https://w3w.co/loudly.maker.extra)

**Upper Ground entrance** – located off Stratford Walk, on Podium Level

Coordinates: 51°32'30.2"N 0°00'48.9"W 
what3words: [tilt.struck.avoid](https://w3w.co/tilt.struck.avoid)

- Stratford underground and overground, National Rail and Stratford International station (all roughly 15 – 20 minutes' walk away)
- Many buses stop nearby at Stratford Station and the surrounding area ([see here](https://tfl.gov.uk/maps/bus?Input=London+E20+2AR%2C+UK&InputGeolocation=51.54163360595703%2C-0.013055800460278988))
- There is no bike parking directly in front of the museum, but there is some available to the side and at the back of the building, near Carpenters Road.
- There is no parking provided or managed by the V&A. However, there is public Blue Badge parking on Carpenters Road, which is available on a first-come, first-served basis and cannot be booked.

Plan your journey with [Transport For London](https://tfl.gov.uk/).

Follow [this useful step-by-step guide](https://www.vam.ac.uk/info/va-east-museum-visual-story) to get from Stratford underground station to V&A East Museum. 

Parking cars nearby is limited, so we advise using public transport. The nearest parking spaces are at Westfield Stratford City.

## Access

The nearest step-free access station is Stratford, which is a 15 – 20 minute walk away.

There is public Blue Badge parking on Carpenters Road, which is available on a first-come, first-served basis and cannot be booked.

Our two entrances are step-free and wheelchair accessible.

You can borrow a wheelchair during your visit. We recommend booking these at least 24 hours in advance. You can also ask a member of staff when you arrive, on a first-come, first-served basis.

[Book a wheelchair](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=pqhybT5ixEK4FwRbTfKt1Gsoxo2wkT1Mnx1QqCAK_5ZUQjhNTlRBV0xWVU1TRjVSOTVGN1M3WjBOVCQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl)

Disabled visitors are entitled to discounted exhibition tickets. You can add a free companion or carer ticket to every disabled ticket. [Find out What's On and book online.](https://www.vam.ac.uk/whatson?venue=east-museum)

## Gallery closures

Level 3 Gallery will be closed between 11.00 and 19.00 on Saturday 7 November. The terrace will still be accessible to the public.

## Facilities

### Toilets

Accessible toilets are located on each floor, and baby changing facilities are available.

Our Changing Places toilet is on the upper ground floor. It has a hoist and is larger than a standard accessible toilet. If you need to borrow a RADAR key, ask a member of staff.

### Buggy park

​Buggy parking is available located on the Lower Ground floor. Personal belongings are left at your own risk.

### Lifts

Passenger lifts are located on each floor.

### Shops

There are two shops, located on the Upper Ground and 2nd floors. The shops are open during museum opening hours. **Please note, we only accept card payments in our shops**. You can also [shop online](https://www.vam.ac.uk/shop/).

We proudly champion UK designers and manufacturers, as well as supporting artisans and social enterprises from all over the world.

The V&A is a charity and every purchase made in our shops helps to support us.

### Food

Cafe Jikoni is open during museum hours and serves an all-day offer, with grab & go and sit-down dining available, as well as children’s options to choose from.

Visitors are welcome to carry bottled water in our galleries.

You are also welcome to bring cold food and drink to eat on site in the circulation areas.

### Lockers and luggage

There are free storage lockers available for use on a first-come, first-served basis.

Luggage with wheels or large bags are not allowed in the galleries. There are free lockers that can store cabin sized cases, but availability is very limited.

### Quiet space

We have a private quiet space available for anyone who may require it.

## Places to stay

Stay at our neighbouring hotels during your stay in east London, conveniently located for you to enjoy your visit to V&A East.

The V&A is grateful to our Hotel Corporate Members for their support:

## Members

We rely on our Members' continued support to fund our work with young people and local communities at V&A East Museum, transforming access to our collections, as well as helping to fund conservation, research, scholarships, and other important projects.

V&A Members enjoy free and unlimited entry to all exhibitions, a sought-after programme of members' events, a complimentary subscription to The V&A Magazine, and always get at least 10% off in V&A shops. # Graves Gallery

### The Graves Gallery is now closed

#### The Graves Gallery is unable to welcome visitors or house the city's art collection due to a failure in the heating system which cannot be repaired.

We’re committed to securing a bright future for the Gallery and are continuing to work with Sheffield City Council on plans for a major transformation of the Graves Gallery and Central Library building that will see the art collection return home.

In the meantime, we’re looking forward to welcoming you to a new, interim showcase for the collection which will open in the Heart of the City in 2027. 

For the latest updates visit our News pages

# Millennium Gallery

### The Millennium Gallery brings the best in art and design to Sheffield

#### The gallery’s changing exhibition programme showcases the best in national and international art and design alongside the region’s remarkable creative talents. You’ll also find collection displays celebrating Sheffield’s metalworking prowess and the remarkable art and artefacts brought to the city by the artist and writer, John Ruskin.

Sheffield’s Metalwork Collection is one of the finest in the world. You’ll see over 800 examples of the cutlery, flatware and tableware that have made the city famous, as well as beautiful objects collected from every continent.

The gallery is also home to the Guild of St George’s unique Ruskin Collection. Spanning art, illustrated manuscripts and minerals, the collection was established in the 1800s to inspire the people of Sheffield. Today, it’s showcased through regularly changing displays celebrating the contemporary relevance of Ruskin’s visionary ideas.

During your visit, you can enjoy great coffee and some truly fantastic grilled cheese sandwiches in our café, Ambulo. 

And we'll let you into a little secret – the Millennium Gallery has some of the best shopping in Sheffield. If it's a gift you're after, the Gallery shop has just what you need, from must-have homeware and hand-crafted jewellery to books, cards and stationery. 

#### Please donate £5 when you visit and help bring the very best in art and design to Sheffield for people to enjoy on their doorstep.

### Free Entry | Please Donate £5

### Good Morning: A Day in Art by Chantal Joffe & Ishbel Myerscough

**15 Oct 2026 – 17 Jan 2027**  **|  Millennium Gallery**

_Good Morning_ sees acclaimed artists Chantal Joffe and Ishbel Myerscough present their own deeply personal paintings and drawings alongside over 80 works from Sheffield’s collection to trace the unfolding of a single day.

**Free Exhibition  |  [Please Donate £5](https://www.sheffieldmuseums.org.uk/support-us/donate-today/)**

### New Editions: Contemporary Printmaking

**12 Sep – 24 Dec 2026**  **|  Millennium Gallery**

Curated by artists James Green and Ed Bradbury (also know as Kid Acne), this exhibition showcases work by around 60 leading printmakers from across the country. 

And great news if you know a print lover too – editions of all the works are all available in the gallery shop, while stocks last.

### Ruskin Collection : Storm Cloud – The Look of the Sky

**Until 29 Nov 2026**  **|  Millennium Gallery**

In 1884, John Ruskin delivered one of the first lectures to discuss climate change and make a link to industrial pollution. _Storm-Cloud_ explores the legacy of his groundbreaking observations.

**Free Exhibition  |  [Please Donate £5](https://www.sheffieldmuseums.org.uk/support-us/donate-today/)**

# Wedgwood

- [Features](https://www.vam.ac.uk/collections/wedgwood#features)
- [Collection highlights](https://www.vam.ac.uk/collections/wedgwood#highlights)
- [Shop](https://www.vam.ac.uk/collections/wedgwood#shop)

Staffordshire potter and entrepreneur Josiah Wedgwood (1730 – 95) was a pioneering tastemaker, marketeer and social campaigner. In 1759, Josiah founded his ceramics company which achieved global success and remains in production today. Designs and wares saved by the factory and Wedgwood family grew into one of the most important industrial collections in the world. Comprising over 175,000 works of art, ceramics, manuscripts and photographs, the V&A Wedgwood Collection documents production up to the present day, showcasing innovations in taste and fashion spanning over 260 years. 

From Josiah Wedgwood’s Portland Vase, to designs by Eric Ravilious and Daisy Makeig-Jones, the collection and UNESCO-recognised archives showcase the commercial and design history of Wedgwood ceramics. Following a successful fundraising campaign spearheaded by Art Fund the V&A Wedgwood Collection was gifted to the V&A in 2014. 

[Search “Wedgwood” in Explore the Collections](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/search/?q=Wedgwood)

## There is something for everyone at Salford Museum & Art Gallery!

From our recreated Victorian street, Lark Hill Place to ever changing exhibition programme, school holiday activities to adult craft workshops, there really is something for everyone!

For families

We strive to be family friendly throughout, with accessible ways of engaging with our collections and lots of hands-on activities.

[Plan your family visit](https://salfordmuseum.com/visit/families/)

Visit our Local History Library

Our popular library is open Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday and offers both drop-in and [bookable sessions](https://salfordmuseum.com/whats-on/).

It holds a huge collection of photographs, documents and newspapers relating to Salford’s past. It is increasingly popular for family history research, delving into the history of the houses, school projects and community heritage in Salford.

Looking for maps and photographs of old Salford? Researching your family tree? Our local history library will have something for you!

[Local History Library](https://salfordmuseum.com/location/local-history-library/)

Café

Our ground floor café overlooks the beautiful Peel Park and the University of Salford’s Peel Building. It’s the ideal place to meet colleagues, study or socialise with family and friends.

Opening Times: Weekdays from 9.30am – 4.00pm, weekends from 11.30am – 4.00pm

[Café](https://salfordmuseum.com/location/cafe/)

Yorkshire Sculpture International is a partnership between Henry Moore Institute, The Hepworth Wakefield, Leeds Art Gallery and Yorkshire Sculpture Park, celebrating Yorkshire as a hub for sculptural excellence.

## Welcome to Warrington Museum & Art Gallery

Located in Warrington’s Cultural Quarter, Warrington Museum & Art Gallery is one of the oldest civic museums in the UK. Our Grade II listed building has been home to our collections since 1857.

Our diverse displays include fine art, world cultures, natural history, archaeology and local stories of Warrington, alongside engaging temporary exhibitions and community-focused events.

The museum is a welcoming space for discovery, creativity and reflection on local and global heritage.

# Temple Newsam

Visit us to discover the house, farm, and play barn.

[Discover upcoming events](https://museumsandgalleries.leeds.gov.uk/whats-on-at-temple-newsam-tjwc 'Discover upcoming events')

**VISITOR NOTICE**

**Entry to Temple Newsam House is by [guided tour](https://my.leedstickethub.co.uk/events?kid=246&view=calendar&_gl=1*1hnvx0p*_gcl_au*MTM4MzAxNTA2OS4xNzkwMDAyNDYx*_ga*MTExMDUzMTU4NC4xNzc0MjYzNTU5*_ga_VHHGE20MBR*czE3OTQyOTk0NzQkbzQ2NiRnMSR0MTc5NDMwMzk4MSRqNjAkbDAkaDA.*_ga_3TXB0RK29T*czE3OTQyOTk0NzQkbzQ2NiRnMSR0MTc5NDMwMzk4MSRqNjAkbDAkaDA.*_ga_DXKXBX8Q77*czE3OTQyOTk0NzQkbzQ2NiRnMSR0MTc5NDMwMzk4MSRqNjAkbDAkaDA.) in winter.** Please check [Christmas at Temple Newsam](https://museumsandgalleries.leeds.gov.uk/christmas-at-temple-newsam-rg17) for information about December events and opening times.

**14 & 15 November**: House closed to general visitors. Free for [Baby Week](https://museumsandgalleries.leeds.gov.uk/whats-on/leeds-baby-week-takeover-at-temple-newsam-qf6t) attendees.

**Parking:** Elm Tree Walk, the private road within the estate, is now closed to all motor vehicles.Please use the West Entrance on Temple Newsam Road (from the Halton direction) to reach House Car Parks 1 and 2. The North Entrance (via Whitkirk / Colton Road) provides access to the Farm Car Park. Blue Badge parking is available in all car parks.

## Current Events and Upcoming Exhibitions

You've built a sandcastle, had a ride on the donkeys and now its time to visit the Museum and the art galleries ...

... bring us an ice cream please!

[See what's on](https://scarboroughmuseumsandgalleries.org.uk/whats-on/)

## Dive In! 400 Years of Water, Wellness and Seaside Fun

26 September 2026—3 July 2027

Scarborough Art Gallery

Part of the Scarborough 400 celebrations, 'Dive In!' is an exhibition celebrating 400 years since Scarborough’s famous spa water was discovered.

[More info](https://scarboroughmuseumsandgalleries.org.uk/whats-on/event/dive-in-400-years-of-water-wellness-and-seaside-fun/)

## 400 Reasons

From Saturday 26th September 2026

Woodend Gallery

A bright and bold response to a very simple question - “Why Do You Like Scarborough?”

[More info](https://scarboroughmuseumsandgalleries.org.uk/whats-on/event/400-reasons-exhibition/)

## Festive Donkey Trail

2 November 2026—31 December 2026

Rotunda Museum, Scarborough Art Gallery and Woodend Gallery

Look high and low for clues to complete the trail.

[More info](https://scarboroughmuseumsandgalleries.org.uk/whats-on/event/festive-donkey-trail/)

## Visit our café at Woodend

Take time out during your visit with us at **Sitwell Nibbles café**, to enjoy a mouth watering menu of sweet eats, savoury bites and hot and cold drinks.

The café is located in the former Sitwell family dining room, where the family, which included novelists and poets Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell, used to spend their summers in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

[Pop in for a brew](https://scarboroughmuseumsandgalleries.org.uk/visit/woodend-gallery-and-studios/)

 [A row of multicoloured wooden sticks](https://scarboroughmuseumsandgalleries.org.uk/project/a-space-to-be/)

## [A Space To Be](https://scarboroughmuseumsandgalleries.org.uk/project/a-space-to-be/)

Working creatively and with communities in mind, is an important part of our practice at Scarborough Museums and Galleries. Learn more about the free, friendly and fun space at Scarborough Art Gallery.

[Find out more](https://scarboroughmuseumsandgalleries.org.uk/project/a-space-to-be/)

 [A small taxidermied deer in a glass cabinet.](https://www.fromlocaltoglobal.co.uk/)

## [From Local to Global](https://www.fromlocaltoglobal.co.uk/)

A project that explores the collection of Colonel James Harrison, a wealthy landowner and big game hunter who spent his extensive leisure time travelling the British Empire and beyond.

[Go to the project website](https://www.fromlocaltoglobal.co.uk/)

jsonLd.description: Saturday 12 September 2026 – Sunday 3 January 2027 | Worcester City Art Gallery and Museum  Reflections is an invitation to immerse yourself in the fluid beauty and immense power of water. The River Severn, the longest river in the UK, has shaped Worcester's identity and industrial heritage for centuries - and continues to today.  Curated with artists Wayne Warren and Jonathan Wright, Reflections features significant works on loan from the National Gallery and Glynn Vivian Gallery including works by Eugène Boudin, Charles-François Daubigny, Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot and Claude Monet, who all experimented with and mastered the art of capturing light, water and shifting reflections. Reflections inspires the imagination and serves as a reminder of the human responsibility to protect the seas, rivers, streams and waterways that are vital for the future.  As an accredited museum, Oriel Môn holds a fascinating and diverse collection of objects and artefacts.

## History

Establishing and building Oriel Môn

In 1981, Isle of Anglesey County Council acquired the studio collection of Charles Tunnicliffe, who died in 1979. The artist had lived at Malltraeth, Anglesey since moving there from his native Cheshire in 1947.

It was through the efforts of the council, together with the determination of devotees of his work, that this collection was purchased in its entirety and safeguarded for the island’s residents and its visitors.

Following this acquisition, it was decided that a permanent home was required for the collection.

Curator Denise Morris led a team in successfully establishing Oriel Môn - a purpose-built museum and gallery which opened in 1991 to collect and exhibit art and artefacts relating to Anglesey.

As well as Charles Tunnicliffe’s collection, there are also significant art collections of work by Sir Kyffin Williams and the Massey sisters, as well as well-known Welsh artists including Claudia Williams, Gwilym Pritchard and Peter Prendergast.

In 2008, Oriel Môn expanded, with the addition of a gallery - Oriel Kyffin Williams that can exhibit items from national collections.

The gallery was funded through the sale of a limited edition run of prints based on Kyffin Williams’ drawings, funding from its governing body - Isle of Anglesey County Council, donations by the public through the Kyffin Williams Trust and the Arts Council of Wales.

## **One Hall, Many Stories…**

Towneley Hall Museum & Art Gallery was home to the Towneley family for over 600 years. The Hall was purchased by Burnley Corporation, now Burnley Borough Council, in 1902 and has been open to the public as a museum and art gallery since 1903. During that time, the collections have grown to encompass many different subject areas, including fine art, ancient Egypt, local history, and wildlife. Traces of the Towneley family and their staff can still be felt around the Hall, with some spaces having changed very little since the last family member, Alice, Lady O’Hagan left the Hall.

As well as the permanent collections, Towneley hosts a changing programme of contemporary exhibitions and events throughout the year.

# Christmas and New Year

Perth Art Gallery will be closed for Christmas & New Year from **Tuesday 22 December 2026** until **Wednesday 6 January 2027**. The gallery will reopen at **10am on Thursday 7 January 2027**.

## Perth 
Art 
Gallery

Perth Art Gallery is one of Scotland’s most historic cultural venues and home to one of the UK’s oldest public art collections, featuring works by influential modern Scottish artists, including Joan Eardley, Sir William MacTaggart, Calum Colvin, and Alison Watt. Work by JD Fergusson and Margaret Morris is on display, alongside a new collection by JE Millais. The gallery offers family activities, a shop, a coffee bar, and toilets.

## Permanent Displays

Modern Scots, showcases the works of influential modern Scottish artists and their contributions to 20th and 21st-century art. In the Sculpture Court, artworks from 16th to 17th century Europe are also on display. 

For families with children, there’s a popular interactive and playful area, Hands on Art. Perth Art Gallery also houses a coffee bar, toilets, and an Art Gallery Shop.

## The JD Fergusson and Margaret Morris Collection

Celebrating the life and creative partnership of the Scottish Colourist, John Duncan Fergusson, and his partner, Margaret Morris, the pioneering dancer, Fergus and Meg: A Creative Partnership was generously funded by the JD Fergusson Art Foundation.

[Fergus and Meg: A Creative Partnership](https://www.culturepk.org.uk/museums/exhibitions-and-displays/fergus-and-meg-a-creative-partnership/)

## Museum Collections

We care for over 500,000 objects and specimens from around the world.

[Find Out More](https://www.culturepk.org.uk/museums/museum-collections)

## More

#### Our Staff

All staff are identifiable by their Culture Perth and Kinross lanyards. There is a Visitor Assistant Supervisor on site whenever we are open to the public, to ensure that you have a safe and enjoyable visit.

We will not tolerate abuse or violence towards any visitor, contractor, or member of staff.

#### Safety and Security

Keep an eye on your personal belongings throughout your visit. Unattended items may be taken to the Lost and Found for safekeeping.

If you lose something, please inform a Visitor Experience team member for assistance.

Perth Art Gallery prioritises your safety. We have a dedicated Visitor Experience team readily available throughout the gallery to answer questions and provide assistance.

#### Visiting with Children

Families and children of all ages are welcome at Perth Art Gallery.

Perth Art Gallery is a Breastfeeding Friendly Scotland venue committed to creating a supportive environment that welcomes all parents who wish to feed their babies.

Baby changing facilities are available in the male and female toilets at the Gallery.

There are areas where buggies can be parked inside the Gallery.

Emergency nappy changing bags are available.  Please ask a member of staff if you require a bag.

#### Hands On Art

Hands On Art is Perth Art Gallery’s dedicated interactive space, designed for young children. It fosters exploration and play and builds confidence in an art gallery environment.

Whether it is your child’s first time visiting a gallery or their hundredth, this is the ideal place to create, touch, and discover. Read more [**here**](https://www.culturepk.org.uk/museums/exhibitions-and-displays/hands-on-art/).

We will also regularly have programmes and workshops, so keep an eye on our ‘[What is On](https://www.culturepk.org.uk/what-is-on/)‘ page for all the latest events at Perth Art Gallery, or follow us on Instagram or Facebook to stay up to date.

#### Baby Play

Baby Play is a relaxed baby group session of colour, sound, and touch where tiny hands explore soft textures, soothing melodies, and playful rhythms.

It’s a space where art comes alive through the rustle of fabric, the sparkle of light, and the joy of song and movement. Like a living painting, each session invites little ones to build up their play skills using the magic of connection through the senses.

After the session has ended, everyone can enjoy our play-inspired, **[Hands On Art](https://www.culturepk.org.uk/museums/exhibitions-and-displays/hands-on-art/)** area at their leisure.

Discover our session dates [**here**](https://www.culturepk.org.uk/recurring/mini-play-for-babies/).

#### Messy Play

Get creative as a family and come and join us for some play through art! Play, explore, and create art in our fun sessions for children under 5 (older siblings are welcome) and their grown-ups. Each month, we will explore a famous artist together through a drop-in session. Have fun creating in the making area together, explore our Hands On Art area, and move through our current exhibitions as you wish. A relaxed and informal time for the family at the gallery.

Discover our session dates [**here**](https://www.culturepk.org.uk/recurring/mini-messy-play-for-families/).

#### Food & Drink

Did you know that you can enjoy delicious, **Fairtrade**, ethically sourced coffee in the foyer at Perth Art Gallery?

The Coffee Cart has various hot and cold drinks, including espresso, americano, latte, flat white, cappuccino, as well as speciality tea, available for visitors to purchase for sitting in and takeaway. The Coffee Cart also offers cold food options, including crisps, traybakes, and individually wrapped cakes.

**Perth Art Gallery is closed on Tuesday and Wednesday.**

#### How to get here

**Train**

Walking from Perth Railway Station should take just under 20 minutes through the city centre.

**Bus**

The nearest bus stop to Perth Art Gallery is located on [George Street](https://maps.app.goo.gl/5xRCuqvfhoVXnyRRA). The following buses stop here – 3, 3A, 7, 7A, 11, 11A, 11S, 12, 57A.

**Walking**

Perth Art Gallery is located in Perth city centre and is within walking distance of many shops and amenities.  It is also 5 minute walk from the North Inch.

**Cycle**

You can cycle to Perth Art Gallery, and there are bicycle stalls outside the Gallery for securing bicycles.  More information [here](https://www.google.com/maps/dir//Perth+Art+Gallery,+George+Street,+Perth/@56.3982599,-3.510905,12z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m9!4m8!1m0!1m5!1m1!1s0x48863b124b004549:0x7a3962a9df235732!2m2!1d-3.4283336!2d56.3982873!3e1?hl=en&entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDQxMy4wIKXMDSoJLDEwMjExNjM5SAFQAw%3D%3D).

**Car**

There is no parking at the venue however there is a variety of pay and display, multi-storey and on street parking nearby to suit your needs.  More information can be found [here](https://www.pkc.gov.uk/article/14739/Parking-in-Perth-City-Centre).

#### Lost Property

We keep any lost property items for a maximum of 30 days. If an item has not been claimed within 30 days, we will dispose of it. We are happy to return items to their original owners; however, there will be a cost for postage and packaging.

#### Travel Trade and Large Group Visits

We welcome visits to Perth Art Gallery from organised tour groups and travel operators and can work with you to develop bespoke packages to meet the needs and interests of your client group.

Self-Directed tours are also welcomed.

For more information and to discuss how we can help give your clients an exceptional experience in the heart of one of the oldest cities in Scotland, please contact us via traveltrade@culturepk.org.uk

Visit our dedicated Travel Trade page [here](https://www.culturepk.org.uk/museums/travel-trade-at-perth-art-gallery/).

#### Accessibility

The entrance on George Street is accessible by steps or a ramp with automatic doors to the entrance vestibule. Within the entrance vestibule there are three further steps which lead into the main entrance hall with automatic doors. Within the entrance vestibule, a platform lift is also available. There is a disabled toilet, hearing loop and seats throughout the gallery. Free wheelchair hire is available, however this is subject to availability and we recommend calling [01738 783400](tel:%2001738%20783400) on the day of your visit.

Assistance dogs are always welcome in Perth Art Gallery.  Fresh water is available.

Noise cancelling headphones can be borrowed at the reception desk.

### Exhibitions and Displays

Discover the permanent collections at Perth Art Gallery, home of the JD Fergusson and Margaret Morris Collection, Millais in Perthshire, the Dark Room Photography, Modern Scots and Hands on Art, our family friendly space, all free to access.

## F.E. McWilliam Gallery

The F.E. McWilliam Gallery and Studio is dedicated to the memory of sculptor Frederick Edward McWilliam, one of Ireland’s most influential and successful artists. F.E. McWilliam was born in Banbridge on the 30th April 1909. He died in London in 1992 and the executors of his estate donated the sculptor’s studio and its contents to the town of his birth.

Featuring a permanent display of McWilliam’s work, temporary exhibitions of Irish and international art, a craft shop, café and the F.E. McWilliam Gallery and Studio attracts a wide range of local, national and international visitors.
